title: Inside the skill
caption: Domain knowledge can live inside a skill, kept apart from the steps until a step needs it.

disclosure.text: the AI opens each supporting file only when a step needs it. <marker><link>See Slide 4</link></marker>.

domain.text: true in every project, like a species guide.

project.text: true for one, like today's depth.

steps.check-camera: Check the camera for loose sediment.
steps.label: Label the sample.

long.text: Wipe the rim first and check the cap's ring for grit.

pointers.label: Fill in the label template.

rules.head: Two rules for long files
rules.contents: <marker>Long reference files start with a contents list, because the AI may only read the start.</marker>
rules.long: <marker>When the instructions get long, move the next paragraph into a reference file.</marker>

tree: <marker>The skill’s folder, every file one level under SKILL.md</marker>

move-detail-out-of-skill-md-and-say-when.header: Move detail out of SKILL.md, and say when to read it
move-detail-out-of-skill-md-and-say-when.description: "Keep your main SKILL.md under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to separate files" [1]. The key is telling the agent when to load each file, for example "Read references/api-errors.md if the API returns a non-200 status code" [2].

agent-skills-best-practices.title: Agent Skills, Best practices for skill creators

long-reference-files-start-with-a-conten.header: Long reference files start with a contents list
long-reference-files-start-with-a-conten.description: "For reference files longer than 100 lines, include a table of contents at the top. This ensures Claude can see the full scope of available information even when previewing with partial reads" [1]. This is Anthropic's account of Claude's behaviour and no source measures its effect.

references-stay-one-level-deep.description: Claude "might partially read files when they're referenced from other referenced files", using commands such as head -100, so references stay one level deep from SKILL.md [1]. The standard states the rule without the reason [2].

progressive-disclosure-as-anthropic-name.header: Progressive disclosure, as Anthropic names it
progressive-disclosure-as-anthropic-name.description: Anthropic's docs say the filesystem-based design "allows progressive disclosure: Claude loads information in stages as needed, rather than consuming context upfront" [1]. Supporting files opened only at the step that needs them are the same idea as the three loading levels.

footer.analogy: The card in its sleeve: each extra tied to the step that uses it.
footer.chat: <marker>When step 4 opens the species guide, its contents page alone tells the AI what else is inside.</marker>
footer.coding: Link every supporting file straight from SKILL.md, one level deep.

alt.scene: The procedure card in its sleeve on the control-room wall: six steps, step 4 lit. Step 3 points to a script, the arm preset; step 4 to a reference file, the species guide, which has slid out of the sleeve open on its contents page; step 6 to a template, the label template. Step 5 runs long and points to the rule for long instructions.

extras-by-step.title: Extras by step
extras-by-step.script: So what can safely live inside a skill? Domain knowledge, kept in supporting files and tied to the step that needs it. Step three, lower the arm, runs a script, the arm preset. Step four, identify what you collected, reads a reference file, the species guide, and step six, label the sample, fills in a template.

the-long-step.title: The long step
the-long-step.script: When one step's instructions grow long, move the next paragraph into a reference file and leave a pointer in the step, so the instructions stay short enough for the model to take in at once.

contents-first.title: Contents first
contents-first.script: And start every long reference file with a contents list, because the model may only skim the top. When step four opens the species guide, its contents page alone tells the model what else is inside.
